project.name: Biobank Biosample and Data Integration Metadata Schema
project.desc: The Biobank Biosample and Data Integration Metadata Schema extends the MOLGENIS FAIR Genomes framework to standardise how biobank catalogues describe biological samples and their associated large-scale datasets. It links donor profiles, consent, and biospecimen records directly to multi-omics and imaging data using established ontologies. This structured approach facilitates seamless sample discovery, data harmonisation, and metadata exchange across biobank networks.
project.author: Radoslava Kacová
K. Joeri van der Velde
Morris A. Swertz

dataset.name: Biobank Biosample and Data Integration Metadata Schema
dataset.desc: The Biobank Biosample and Data Integration Metadata Schema extends the MOLGENIS FAIR Genomes framework to standardise how biobank catalogues describe biological samples and their associated large-scale datasets. It links donor profiles, consent, and biospecimen records directly to multi-omics and imaging data using established ontologies. This structured approach facilitates seamless sample discovery, data harmonisation, and metadata exchange across biobank networks.

concept.name: Analysis
concept.desc: Computational and bioinformatic processing workflows applied to primary sequencing data, including reference genome alignment, variant calling algorithms, standard pipeline guidelines, and stored output file formats.

concept.name: Algorithms used
concept.desc: Any used problem-solving procedures implemented in software to be executed by a computer.

concept.name: Analysis identifier
concept.desc: A unique proper name or character sequence that identifies this particular analysis.

concept.name: Belongs to sequencing
concept.desc: Reference to the sequencing that was performed, i.e. the source on which this analysis was based.

concept.name: Bioinformatic protocol used
concept.desc: A human-readable collection of information about about how a scientific experiment or analysis was carried out that results in a specific set of data or results used for further analysis or to test a specific hypothesis.

concept.name: Data formats stored
concept.desc: Which data file formats (i.e. defined ways or layouts of representing and structuring data in a computer file, blob, string, message, or elsewhere) are stored and potentially available.

concept.name: Reference genome used
concept.desc: The specific build of the human genome used as reference for sequence alignment and variant calling.

concept.name: Biospecimens
concept.desc: A specific physical unit, aliquot, or processed preparation derived from primary material (e.g. FFPE block, frozen tissue section, biofluid aliquot) managed in biobank storage under defined preservation and fixation conditions.

concept.name: Availability
concept.desc: The current operational or inventory status indicating whether the biospecimen is available for research, reserved, depleted, or destroyed.

concept.name: Biospecimen Form
concept.desc: The specific physical form, fraction, or analyte derived from the parent material (e.g., extracted genomic DNA, total RNA, serum, cell lysate, or FFPE section) prepared for downstream analysis or sequencing.

concept.name: Biospecimen identifier
concept.desc: A unique proper name or character sequence that identifies this particular biospecimen.

concept.name: Derived from material
concept.desc: Identifies the parent biological Material entity from which this biospecimen directly or indirectly originates, either as a physical portion (aliquot) or as a derived fraction (e.g., extracted DNA, serum, tissue section).

concept.name: Embedding medium
concept.desc: A material that infiltrates and supports a specimen and preserves its shape and structure for sectioning and microscopy.

concept.name: Managing biobank
concept.desc: The organization or facility that owns, manages, and physically stores this biospecimen or slide, maintaining custody and responsibility for its storage conditions and associated data.

concept.name: Name of fixative
concept.desc: The name of the compound that preserves tissues and cells for microscopic study.

concept.name: Percentage tumor cells
concept.desc: The percentage of tumor cells compared to total cells present in this material.

concept.name: Quantity
concept.desc: The total count or number of available physical units, aliquots, blocks, or slides representing this specific biospecimen instance.

concept.name: Storage conditions
concept.desc: The environmental temperature and preservation parameter under which the biospecimen is maintained in the repository.

concept.name: Clinical
concept.desc: Clinical observations, diagnoses, disease staging, and longitudinal treatment responses recorded for a patient across specific disease encounters or study timepoints.

concept.name: Age at diagnosis
concept.desc: Age of the patient in years at the time of disease diagnosis.

concept.name: Belongs to person
concept.desc: Reference to the person whom this clinical information is about.

concept.name: Clinical identifier
concept.desc: A unique proper name or character sequence that identifies this particular clinical examination.

concept.name: Clinical timepoint
concept.desc: Relative timepoint or clinical phase of this encounter relative to diagnosis or baseline (e.g. Baseline, Post-treatment, Relapse, Day 0, Month 3).

concept.name: Diagnosis
concept.desc: Main clinical diagnosis coded using ICD-10, ORPHA, or SNOMED CT.

concept.name: Disease stage
concept.desc: Broad categorisation of disease progression at the time of data or sample collection (e.g. Stage I-IV, Early/Advanced, Primary/Metastatic).

concept.name: Molecular diagnosis gene
concept.desc: Causal gene(s) bearing a confirmed pathogenic or clinically significant variant associated with the patient's diagnosis or response to treatment (e.g. BRCA1, EGFR, KRAS). Do not list all tested panel genes here.

concept.name: Response to treatment
concept.desc: The patients' response to the applied treatment regimen.

concept.name: Treatment category
concept.desc: High-level classification of therapies applied to the patient (e.g. Chemotherapy, Radiotherapy, Immunotherapy, Surgery, Naive/Untreated).

concept.name: Computed tomography (CT)
concept.desc: Modality-specific series metadata for computed tomography acquisitions, capturing X-ray tube exposure parameters, spiral pitch, reconstruction convolution kernels, and slice geometry.

concept.name: CT identifier
concept.desc: A unique identifier for CT series of images.

concept.name: Convolution kernel
concept.desc: An algorithm used to reconstruct imaging data. Convolution kernels can be used to filter images to smooth them and reduce noise or to enhance edges or other image features. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,1210).

concept.name: Exposure time (ms)
concept.desc: The cumulative time a subject was exposed to X-rays during image acquisition. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,1150).

concept.name: Field of view
concept.desc: The physical size of the anatomical region covered in the reconstructed image, expressed in millimetres. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,9317).

concept.name: Filter type
concept.desc: Specifies the type of X-ray beam–shaping filter used during image acquisition (e.g., body, head, bowtie, wedge). Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,1160).

concept.name: Imaging injection
concept.desc: Administration of CT contrast medium using an injector device. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,1040).

concept.name: Slice thickness
concept.desc: The dimension between two surfaces of an imaging plane, specified in millimetres (mm). Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,0050).

concept.name: Spiral pitch factor
concept.desc: Ratio of the distance that the table moves during a complete revolution of the source around the gantry orbit, to the width of the total collimation over the area of active x-ray detection (DICOM tag (0018,9311)).

concept.name: Tube voltage (kVp)
concept.desc: The peak accelerating voltage applied in an X-ray tube between the cathode and anode, corresponding to DICOM tag (0018,0060).

concept.name: X_Ray tube current (mA)
concept.desc: The value of the electrical current applied to an X-ray tube (DICOM tag (0018,1151)).

concept.name: Z_axis spacing
concept.desc: The physical spacing between adjacent CT image slices along the Z-axis, representing the voxel dimension in the slice-selection direction. Expressed in millimetres (mm). Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,0088).

concept.name: Digital mammography (MG)
concept.desc: Modality-specific series metadata for digital mammography acquisitions, capturing dedicated breast examination projections and associated radiographic parameters.

concept.name: MG identifier
concept.desc: A unique identifier for MG series of images.

concept.name: Digital radiography (DX)
concept.desc: Modality-specific series metadata for projection digital radiography acquisitions, capturing patient orientation, X-ray tube potential, and exposure settings.

concept.name: DX identifier
concept.desc: A unique identifier for DX series of images.

concept.name: Exposure (mAs)
concept.desc: The exposure expressed in mAs, for example calculated from Exposure Time and X-Ray Tube Current.

concept.name: Patient orientation
concept.desc: Orientation of patient relative to imaging device. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0020,0020).

concept.name: Imaging series
concept.desc: Common metadata and technical characteristics for a coherent series of biomedical image instances acquired using a single equipment, coordinate frame, and imaging modality within an imaging study.

concept.name: Annotations available
concept.desc: Indicates whether annotation data associated with the image (e.g., regions of interest, labels, markup, or segmentation overlays) are present and accessible.

concept.name: Belongs to imaging study
concept.desc: Parent study context.

concept.name: Body region
concept.desc: The specific anatomical region, body part, or organ targeted by this imaging series.

concept.name: Channel resolution
concept.desc: The number of bits used to represent the stored value of each pixel channel. In DICOM, this corresponds to tag (0028,0101).

concept.name: Color space
concept.desc: The photometric interpretation of pixel data that defines the type of colour or greyscale encoding used in the image (e.g., MONOCHROME2, RGB, YBR_FULL). Corresponds to DICOM tag (0028,0004).

concept.name: Compression method
concept.desc: Indicates whether the image was lossy-compressed and which method was used, based on DICOM tags (0028,2110) and (0028,2114).

concept.name: File format
concept.desc: The digital format used to encode and store an imaging file.

concept.name: File size
concept.desc: The size of the file in MB.

concept.name: Image depth
concept.desc: The number of distinct image planes captured during acquisition. For WSI, this represents the number of focal planes (Z-stack levels). For CT, MRI, and PET, it corresponds to the number of cross-sectional slices or frames. For DX and MG, this value is typically 1 (a single 2D projection).

concept.name: Image height
concept.desc: Number of pixels in one column of the image, corresponding to the DICOM attribute Rows (0028,0010).

concept.name: Image type
concept.desc: A classification of the image based on the imaging modality and acquisition characteristics. It specifies the type of image produced during the scan (e.g., T1-weighted MRI, T2-weighted MRI, CT attenuation image, PET uptake image).

concept.name: Image width
concept.desc: Number of pixels in one row of the image, corresponding to the DICOM attribute Columns (0028,0011).

concept.name: Imaging device
concept.desc: A device for producing a representation or picture, usually of a part of the body, to aid in diagnosis and evaluation.

concept.name: Imaging modality
concept.desc: Any technology or method that aids in the visualization of any biological process, cell, tissue or organ for use in screening, diagnosis, surgical procedures or therapy.

concept.name: Laterality
concept.desc: The side of the body or paired organ being examined (e.g. Left, Right, Bilateral, Unilateral).

concept.name: Manufacturer of imaging device
concept.desc: A person, enterprise, or entity that produces imaging device.

concept.name: Number of channels
concept.desc: The number of distinct data channels stored in each pixel of the image. Channels may represent color components (e.g., RGB), grayscale intensity, or modality-specific signal dimensions.

concept.name: Pixel spacing
concept.desc: Physical distance between the centres of adjacent pixels in the image space, specified as row and column spacing. Expressed in millimetres (mm) according to DICOM attribute (0028,0030).

concept.name: Series date
concept.desc: The date on which a series began.

concept.name: Series instance identifier
concept.desc: A unique identifier for series of images.

concept.name: Software version
concept.desc: A form or variant of software; one of a sequence of copies of a software program, each incorporating new modifications.

concept.name: Imaging study
concept.desc: A diagnostic, clinical, or research imaging procedure comprising one or more imaging series (e.g. radiological scans such as CT/MRI or digital pathology whole slide images) acquired for a subject within a common clinical or study context.

concept.name: Affiliated institution
concept.desc: The organisation or institution responsible for performing the imaging study.

concept.name: Images count
concept.desc: The total number of individual image instances or frames comprising this imaging study.

concept.name: Imaging procedure
concept.desc: An imaging procedure as defined by SNOMED CT, representing a specific diagnostic or acquisition procedure (e.g., 'CT of breast', 'MRI of head', or 'Whole Slide Imaging'), rather than the general modality or technique alone. The general modality or technique (e.g., 'CT', 'MR', 'SM') is captured separately in the 'Imaging modality' field.

concept.name: Imaging study identifier
concept.desc: The user- or equipment-generated identifier of an instance of a study entity.

concept.name: Reason for imaging procedure
concept.desc: The clinical or research rationale for performing the imaging procedure. This field captures why the procedure was indicated for the patient, such as screening, diagnosis, treatment planning, or research purposes. It should express the intent or medical reason, not the technical details of the procedure itself.

concept.name: Series count
concept.desc: The total number of image series contained within this imaging study.

concept.name: Study date
concept.desc: The date on which a study began.

concept.name: Individual consent
concept.desc: Record of a signed informed consent given by an individual or legal guardian, specifying data and sample use permissions, restrictions, and validity periods.

concept.name: Allow recontacting
concept.desc: Indication of whether the participant has consented to be re-contacted by the biobank or clinical team for study updates, further sample donations, or actionable secondary health findings.

concept.name: Belongs to study
concept.desc: Reference to the study for which this individual consent permits data and sample use.

concept.name: Collected by
concept.desc: The healthcare facility, clinical ward, or biobank site where the informed consent was administered and obtained.

concept.name: Consent form used
concept.desc: Link to the specific approved template version in the Leaflet and consent form module used during signing.

concept.name: Data use modifiers
concept.desc: Data use modifiers indicate additional conditions for use. For instance, a dataset is restricted to investigations into specific diseases or performed at specific geographical locations.

concept.name: Data use permissions
concept.desc: The primary consented permission and intended scope governing the secondary research use of datasets and biological specimens.

concept.name: Individual consent identifier
concept.desc: A unique proper name or character sequence that identifies this particular signed individual consent.

concept.name: Person consenting
concept.desc: Reference to the person (i.e. subject) to whom this individual consent applies.

concept.name: Represented by
concept.desc: An individual who is authorized under applicable State or local law to consent on behalf of a child or incapable person to general medical care including participation in clinical research.

concept.name: Signing date
concept.desc: A date specification that designates when this individual consent form was signed.

concept.name: Valid until
concept.desc: The expiry date or termination date of the consent, such as upon participant withdrawal or completion of a time-limited study protocol.

concept.name: Leaflet and consent form
concept.desc: Specification and metadata of the informative leaflet and blank informed consent template version approved for a study or biobank collection.

concept.name: Consent form creator
concept.desc: The authoritative biobank institution, hospital, or governance board that authored and issued this consent form.

concept.name: Consent form identifier
concept.desc: A unique persistent identifier, DOI, or resolvable URL unambiguously identifying this specific consent template and leaflet pair.

concept.name: Consent form title
concept.desc: The formal document title of the informed consent form template.

concept.name: Consent form version
concept.desc: The formal version number, release tag, or revision identifier of this consent form template.

concept.name: Magnetic resonance (MR)
concept.desc: Modality-specific series metadata for magnetic resonance imaging acquisitions, capturing static magnetic field strength, radiofrequency pulse sequence timing (TR/TE), flip angle, and receive coil configurations.

concept.name: Echo time
concept.desc: The time in milliseconds between the application of the excitation pulse and the recording of the peak echo signal. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,0081).

concept.name: Flip angle
concept.desc: In magnetic resonance imaging, the angle by which the net magnetization vector is rotated away from the main magnetic field (B₀) by an applied radiofrequency pulse. It is expressed in degrees (°). Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,1314).

concept.name: Imaging frequency
concept.desc: The Larmor resonance frequency used during MR data acquisition, determined by the strength of the static magnetic field (B₀) and expressed in megahertz (MHz). Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,0084).

concept.name: Inversion time
concept.desc: The time between the inversion and excitation pulses in an inversion recovery pulse sequence, expressed in milliseconds (ms). Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,0082).

concept.name: MR identifier
concept.desc: A unique identifier for MR series of images.

concept.name: Magnetic field strength
concept.desc: A measurement of the strength of the static magnetic field (B₀) generated by an MRI system, expressed in units of Tesla (T). Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,0087).

concept.name: Receive coil name
concept.desc: The designated name of the radiofrequency (RF) receive coil used during MR acquisition, identifying the specific hardware component that detects the MR signal. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,1250).

concept.name: Repetition time
concept.desc: The amount of time in milliseconds (ms) between successive pulse sequences applied to the same slice. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,0080).

concept.name: Sequence name
concept.desc: The literal identifier for the pulse sequence. Corresponds to DICOM tag (0018,0024).

concept.name: Material
concept.desc: Primary biological material obtained directly from a donor or patient through a collection procedure (e.g. biopsy, surgery, blood draw), defining the original anatomical source, sampling timestamp, and pathological state.

concept.name: Anatomical source
concept.desc: The specific organ, anatomical site, or bodily structure of the individual from which the biological material was procured.

concept.name: Belongs to diagnosis
concept.desc: Reference to a diagnosis c.q. clinical examination of which this material may be a part of. There can be multiple diagnoses when a non-tumor material is reused as reference.

concept.name: Collected from person
concept.desc: Reference to the person from whom this material was collected.

concept.name: Material identifier
concept.desc: A unique proper name or character sequence that identifies this particular material.

concept.name: Material type
concept.desc: The broad biological nature of the collected substance prior to processing (e.g. whole blood, solid tissue, bone marrow, saliva, urine).

concept.name: Pathological state
concept.desc: The histological or pathological condition of the procured biological specimen or biofluid (e.g. malignant, benign, non-involved control, premalignant).

concept.name: Sampling date
concept.desc: The date that a sample was collected or obtained.

concept.name: Personal
concept.desc: Demographic, phenotypic, and baseline characteristics of an individual study participant or patient from whom biological materials and associated research data are collected.

concept.name: Age at death
concept.desc: In the event of participant decease, the calculated age of the individual at the time of death, measured in completed years.

concept.name: Ancestry
concept.desc: The genetic or geographic ancestral background of an individual, evaluated using ancestry-informative genomic markers or population categories.

concept.name: Country of birth
concept.desc: The country in which the individual was born.

concept.name: Country of residence
concept.desc: The sovereign country where the individual primarily resides at the time of study enrolment or sample collection.

concept.name: Gender at birth
concept.desc: The gender or biological sex assigned to the individual at birth, typically documented in medical records or official birth certificates.

concept.name: Participates in study
concept.desc: Reference to the study or studies in which this person participates.

concept.name: Personal identifier
concept.desc: A unique pseudonymised code or persistent subject identifier assigned to an individual within the study or biobank repository.

concept.name: Primary affiliated institute
concept.desc: The primary healthcare facility, clinical centre, or biobank institution responsible for the medical management or enrolment of the individual.

concept.name: Status
concept.desc: The most recent vital or clinical follow-up status of the individual recorded by the biobank or registry (e.g. alive, deceased, lost to follow-up).

concept.name: Year of birth
concept.desc: The year in which the individual person was born.

concept.name: Sample preparation
concept.desc: The pre-analytical laboratory procedure used to extract, isolate, and prepare nucleic acids into sequencing libraries, including target enrichment, molecular barcoding, and library quality control.

concept.name: Fully sequenced genes
concept.desc: List of genes where the entire coding sequence (all exons) was targeted and sequenced.

concept.name: Input amount
concept.desc: Amount of input material in nanogram (ng).

concept.name: Intended insert size
concept.desc: In paired-end sequencing, the DNA between the adapter sequences is the insert. The length of this sequence is known as the insert size, not to be confused with the inner distance between reads. So, fragment length equals read adapter length (2x) plus insert size, and insert size equals read lenght (2x) plus inner distance.

concept.name: Intended read length
concept.desc: The number of nucleotides intended to be ordered from each side of a nucleic acid fragment obtained after the completion of a sequencing process.

concept.name: Library preparation kit
concept.desc: Pre-filled, ready-to-use reagent cartridges intented to improve chemistry, cluster density and read length as well as improve quality (Q) scores for this sample. Reagent components are encoded to interact with the sequencing system to validate compatibility with user-defined applications.

concept.name: PCR free
concept.desc: Indicates whether a polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was used to prepare this sample. PCR is a method for amplifying a DNA base sequence using multiple rounds of heat denaturation of the DNA and annealing of oligonucleotide primers complementary to flanking regions in the presence of a heat-stable polymerase.

concept.name: Partially sequenced genes
concept.desc: List of genes where only specific regions or hotspots (selected exons/codons) were targeted and sequenced.

concept.name: Sampleprep identifier
concept.desc: A unique proper name or character sequence that identifies this particular sample preparation.

concept.name: Target enrichment kit
concept.desc: Indicates which target enrichment kit was used to prepare this sample. Target enrichment is a pre-sequencing DNA preparation step where DNA sequences are either directly amplified (amplicon or multiplex PCR-based) or captured (hybrid capture-based) in order to only focus on specific regions of a genome or DNA sample.

concept.name: UMIs present
concept.desc: Indicates whether any unique molecular identifiers (UMIs) are present. An UMI barcode is a short nucleotide sequence that is used to identify reads originating from an individual mRNA molecule.

concept.name: Sequencing
concept.desc: Technical execution and instrument run parameters of a high-throughput sequencing assay, including sequencer platform, read metrics, coverage depth, and sequencing quality control statistics.

concept.name: Belongs to sample preparation
concept.desc: Reference to the prepared sample, i.e. the source that was sequenced.

concept.name: Median read depth
concept.desc: The median number of times a particular locus (site, nucleotide, amplicon, region) was sequenced.

concept.name: Observed insert size
concept.desc: In paired-end sequencing, the DNA between the adapter sequences is the insert. The length of this sequence is known as the insert size, not to be confused with the inner distance between reads. So, fragment length equals read adapter length (2x) plus insert size, and insert size equals read lenght (2x) plus inner distance.

concept.name: Observed read length
concept.desc: The number of nucleotides successfully ordered from each side of a nucleic acid fragment obtained after the completion of a sequencing process.

concept.name: Other quality metrics
concept.desc: Other NGS quality control metrics, including but not limited to (i) sequencer metrics such as yield, error rate, density (K/mm2), cluster PF (%) and phas/prephas (%), (ii) alignment metrics such as QM insert size, GC content, QM duplicated reads (%), QM error rate, uniformity/evenness of coverage and maternal cell contamination, and (iii) variant call metrics such as number of SNVs/CNVs/SVs called, number of missense/nonsense variants, common variants (%), unique variants (%), gender match and trio inheritance check.

concept.name: Percentage Q30
concept.desc: Percentage of reads with a Phred quality score over 30, which indicates less than a 1/1000 chance that the base was called incorrectly.

concept.name: Percentage TR20
concept.desc: Percentage of the target sequence on which 20 or more unique reads were successfully mapped.

concept.name: Sequencing date
concept.desc: Date on which this sequencing assay was performed.

concept.name: Sequencing identifier
concept.desc: A unique proper name or character sequence that identifies this particular nucleic acid sequencing assay.

concept.name: Sequencing instrument model
concept.desc: The used product name and model number of a manufacturer's genomic (dna) sequencer.

concept.name: Sequencing method
concept.desc: Method used to determine the order of bases in a nucleic acid sequence.

concept.name: Sequencing platform
concept.desc: The used sequencing platform (i.e. brand, name of a company that produces sequencer equipment).

concept.name: Slide preparation assay
concept.desc: A laboratory protocol for preparing, sectioning, and staining biological specimens on glass slides (e.g. histological, special staining, or immunohistochemistry assays) prior to whole slide imaging or microscopic evaluation.

concept.name: Antibody name
concept.desc: The vendor-stated name of an antibody used to detect and visualize the presence of an antigen.

concept.name: Assay identifier
concept.desc: An assay identifier is an identifier that identifies some assay (analysis).

concept.name: Assay type
concept.desc: The specific type of laboratory test or analytical procedure performed on a bio-specimen mounted on a glass slide. It defines the staining or labeling technique applied to the specimen to reveal specific structural, molecular, or cellular features.

concept.name: Belongs to biospecimen
concept.desc: Reference to the biospecimen (e.g. FFPE block, slide) that was the physical input to this slide preparation assay.

concept.name: Biomarker spatial localization
concept.desc: The subcellular or structural location within a tissue or cell where the biomarker is expressed or detected.

concept.name: Biomarker type
concept.desc: A classification of the type of biomolecule or biological component that the assay targets, labels, or detects. It characterizes whether the biomarker is, for example, a protein, nucleic acid, carbohydrate, lipid, or inorganic substance.

concept.name: Counter labeling
concept.desc: The counter-labeling technique used to highlight specific cellular or tissue structures, serving as a complementary method to the primary labeling for analysis

concept.name: Dye name
concept.desc: The neutral or synthetic colored substance used for staining specific tissues or cellular components.

concept.name: Pathogen type
concept.desc: Identification of the specific type of pathogen among the listed categories e.g. 'Virus','Viroid','Bacterium'...

concept.name: Precedes the study
concept.desc: Reference to the subsequent imaging study or digital whole-slide scanning event for which this prepared slide serves as the direct physical input.

concept.name: Section thickness
concept.desc: A measurement of the thickness of a sectioned slice (of tissue or mineral or other substance), expressed in micrometers (µm).

concept.name: Study
concept.desc: A research study, trial, or project context under which biological samples and associated datasets are collected, grouped, and managed for specific research objectives.

concept.name: Completion date
concept.desc: The date on which all study protocols are finalized, participant follow-ups conclude, or the primary research objectives are fully met.

concept.name: Contact information
concept.desc: An email address for the purpose of contacting the study contact person.

concept.name: Description
concept.desc: A narrative summary outlining the scientific background, main objectives, and overall scope of the study.

concept.name: Identifier
concept.desc: A unique character string or persistent identifier that unambiguously distinguishes this study.

concept.name: Inclusion criteria
concept.desc: The primary medical, demographic, or genetic eligibility criteria required for a participant to be enrolled in this study.

concept.name: Name
concept.desc: The official title, full name, or public label designating this study or research project.

concept.name: Principal investigator
concept.desc: The primary scientific leader, lead researcher, or designated contact person responsible for the design, execution, and integrity of the study.

concept.name: Start date
concept.desc: The date on which this study began.

concept.name: Study URL
concept.desc: A resolvable web address, digital object identifier (DOI) link, or persistent public repository URL pointing to the study documentation, trial registration, or associated online publication.

concept.name: Study design
concept.desc: The methodological framework and operational protocol specification describing how subjects, biospecimens, and data are structured and collected (e.g. cohort, case-control, longitudinal, cross-sectional).

concept.name: Ultrasound Imaging (US)
concept.desc: Modality-specific series metadata for diagnostic ultrasonography acquisitions, capturing acoustic imaging parameters, anatomical focus, and real-time scanning geometry.

concept.name: US identifier
concept.desc: A unique identifier for US series of images.

concept.name: Whole slide imaging (WSI)
concept.desc: Modality-specific series metadata for high-resolution digital pathology whole slide images, capturing optical scanning modes, lens magnification, illumination parameters, and focal z-stacking.

concept.name: Colour (ICC) profile
concept.desc: A standardised colour profile defined by the International Color Consortium (ICC) that specifies how colours in an image should be interpreted to ensure consistent colour rendering across devices (e.g. sRGB or Gray Gamma 1.8/2.2, GSDF).

concept.name: Compression quality label
concept.desc: A vendor-specific indicator describing the applied level or strength of lossy compression (e.g., quality level or percentage), not defined in DICOM but used in some WSI formats to express perceived compression quality.

concept.name: Distance between focal planes
concept.desc: Distance between acquisition focal planes given in micrometers (µm).

concept.name: Illumination method
concept.desc: The method of optical illumination used to illuminate the specimen during scanning (e.g., brightfield, darkfield, fluorescence, phase contrast).

concept.name: Illumination wavelength
concept.desc: Nominal wavelength of the illuminator expressed in nanometres (nm).

concept.name: Number of focal planes
concept.desc: Number of focal planes along the vertical z-axis used for multiple and extended z-stacking methods.

concept.name: Objective lens magnification
concept.desc: The objective lens magnification used for the acquisition of whole slide images, expressed as a dimensionless optical magnification factor (e.g., 10×, 20×, 40×). This refers only to the lens magnification and not the final stored image encoded by the spatial resolution attribute.

concept.name: Pyramid levels
concept.desc: The number of specific resolution levels of an image pyramid.

concept.name: Scanning operation mode
concept.desc: The scanning procedure used to digitize a glass slide. This attribute does not describe the capabilities of the scanner used for digitization.

concept.name: Tissue scan area
concept.desc: The area of the tissue region that was scanned, expressed in square millimetres (mm²).

concept.name: WSI identifier
concept.desc: A unique identifier for WSI series of images.

concept.name: Z_stacking
concept.desc: A digital image processing method which combines multiple images taken at different focal distances to create a composite image with a greater depth of field than is possible for a single image.

valueSet.name: Inclusioncriteria_Opts
valueSet.desc: Options for The primary medical, demographic, or genetic eligibility criteria required for a participant to be enrolled in this study.

designation.displayName: An inclusion criterion that defines and states a Body Mass Index range, which if met, makes an individual suitable for a given task or participation in a given process.
An inclusion criterion that defines and states an age bracket which, if met, makes an entity suitable for a given task or participation in a given process.

concept.displayName: Bank of Biological Material, Charles University - Hradec Králové

designation.displayName: Biobank at the Charles University Faculty of Medicine in Hradec Kralove (bbmri-eric:ID:CZ_CUNI_HK) was established at The Fingerland Department of Pathology. Majority of patients from whom the specimens are stored fall into one of the following categories: colorectal cancer, breast cancer, ovarian cancer, head&neck cancer, lung cancer, brain tumors. The tumor tissue is cryopreserved at the moment of operation for future analysis of both DNA and RNA. Formalin-fixed and paraffin embedded tissue of corresponding neoplasms is stored as well. The specimens are collected in close cooperation with clinical specialists (surgeons, oncologists, etc.).

concept.displayName: Biobank of Institute of Hematology and Blood Transfusion, Prague

designation.displayName: The Biobank IHBT Prague is focused on collecting the samples of patients with haematological disorders. The samples are processed based on our SOPs and according to the type of biological material and diagnosis. Stored samples are intended for the projects approved by the Expert board of the Biobank IHBT Prague. The biobank is equipped with two automated storage systems ASKION C-line® allowing to store samples in the cryogenic temperatures at down to -185°C. For sample processing and freezing serves the ASKION C-line® work bench.

concept.displayName: Bank of Biological Material, Masaryk Memorial Cancer Institute

designation.displayName: Biobank at MMCI was established to preserve patient-derived specimens such as tumours and blood-derived samples . Its structure comprises of a "long-term storage repository" designed to store a comprehensive set of patient samples such as tumours, adjacent tissues, genomic DNA and serum at surgery, and the "short term storage repository" designed to store serum aliquots from periodic determination of soluble blood tumour markers. Comprehensive clinical data are available through the hospital infromation system to enable further translational and clinical research.

The CELSPAC Biobank started operating in 2020 as part of the RECETOX infrastructure (Masaryk University). The fully automated CELSPAC Biobank is primarily responsible for the processing and systematic storage of biological materials from CELSPAC population studies, which provide the objective information necessary to assess the association between exposure and various health outcomes. Our epidemiological databases are specifically designed to enable data sharing to promote multidisciplinary research on EXPOSOME factors that may affect human health.

concept.displayName: Bank of Biological Material, Palacký University

designation.displayName: The biobank affiliated with University Palacky Olomouc and University Hostpital Olomouc, focused primarily on colorectal carcinoma, lung carcinoma, glioma, prostate carcinoma, and melanoms.

concept.displayName: Bank of Biological Material, Institute of Rheumatology

designation.displayName: The Bank of Biological Material of Institute of Rheumatology in Prague stores biospecimen from nearly 8 000 people and about 50 000 unique collection events covering both affected and healthy people.

concept.displayName: Bank of Biological Material, Charles University - Pilsen

designation.displayName: The Bank of Biological Material (BBM) of the Faculty of Medicine in Plzeň of Charles University has been established in the premises of the Department of Immunochemical Diagnostics of the University Hospital Plzeň. Currently the Biobank is systematically collecting for long term storage serum and plasma samples from patients with oncological diagnosis.

concept.displayName: Medical data repository of Institute of Computer Science, Masaryk University

designation.displayName: Medical research data repositories hosted by Institute of Computer Science at Masaryk University.

concept.displayName: Bank of Biological Material of the First Faculty of Medicine of Charles University, Prague

designation.displayName: The Bank of Biological Material (BBM) of the First Faculty of Medicine of Charles University, Prague is primarily focused on the collection of tumour samples for future cancer research. The BBM collects samples of various types of tissues (tumour, metastases, non-tumour) classified by diagnosis, usually together with blood, serum, plasma, genomic DNA and/or urine samples taken at the time of surgery.

This requirement indicates that use of the data is limited to studies in which different data types about the same individual from different datasets are not combined. Linking data is usually used to compile epidemiological data, leading to a richer dataset. The logic of record linkage is that two or more items of information about a person recorded at different times, and perhaps in different places, may be of greater value when considered together than when either is considered alone. The potential risk is that the data subjects in the dataset become more identifiable.
